notes: Other editors were measured 2026-09-23 00:35–02:55 UTC. cctext was re-measured 22:01–22:05 UTC (small_c 22:15–22:16) on commit c946817 (clean tree; includes forward style cursors and per-frame paint scratch) with `--editors cctext --into --idle 10` (see README). The previous cctext cells (commit 9541c72, 10:27–10:33 UTC; before that 4c655a0) are in git history.

The host is a shared 4-core container. Other agents' builds and sanitizer tests ran during the other-editor round. Per-cell `loadavg_before/after` is in the JSON: small_c, text_3m and json_100m ran at load ~0.2–1.5; json_1g and json_2g at ~2–5, sometimes more. The cctext cells waited for load < 1.5 before starting (text_3m waited ~6 min): text_3m, json_100m, json_1g and json_2g ran at load 0.5–0.8 (1.4 at the start of text_3m). small_c started at load 1.2–1.4 and other agents' builds pushed it to ~2.1–2.4 during the cell in both attempts; the committed small_c cell is the second attempt.
json_2g was stopped at the owner's request after nano. emacs was not run on json_2g. The vim, nvim, helix, kakoune, micro and nano json_2g cells are from that partial round, under host load.

After the other-editor round, the idle wait before each PageDown was lengthened from 50 ms to 150 ms. That fixes an artefact in editors that draw a page in several bursts, where the next page could be counted from a stale frame: see nano json_1g PgDn 0.12 ms, which is not real. Only the cctext cells use the longer wait.
cctext has no PageDown key. Its PgDn column is a burst of 24 wheel notches, one repaint since 4c655a0.

Idle columns (cctext only): 10 s with no input right after open, `--no-blink`. Every cctext run on every fixture recorded 0 context switches, 0 CPU ticks and 0 output writes in that window. A one-off check without `--no-blink` (json_100m, 10 s) also gave 0 wakeups, 0 CPU and 0 writes. The same probe sees nvim wake ~0.4/s on small_c, so the zero is measured, not a probe failure.
